subject: Multi-session mixture models with two detector types

messages.author: 457f09fd976062ac
messages.subject: Multi-session mixture models with two detector types
parts:
Dear Murray,

I'm trying to fit a multi-session (12 sessions) using hcov argument for "Sex", but keep receiving NA's in return. After playing around, I found the problem arises when I add two sessions in which the capture method was foot snares (detector = "single") instead of camera trap (detector = "count") like the other 10 sessions. Out of curiosity, I changed the "detector" of these 2 sessions to see what happens, and, as I expected, the model worked fine when detectors were "count", but returns the same error when I changed them to "multi". Also, instead of using hcov, I tried to add "Sex" as a variable for g0 and sigma, but again I had similar problems in the response (NA's for "esa" values). This error is not a problem with secr's version either, I tried with "4.3.1", "4.3.2", and "4.3.3". 

What's the best way of dealing with that? 
Sorry if my doubt is too simple, it's the first time I work with secr and after some days of reading and R-coding, I found myself in a dead-end.

I attached the summaries to give a better idea of what I have in hands, as well as the results using "Sex" in the three ways - hcov, g0, and sigma.

I appreciate any insight you could give me.
Many thanks.
Guilherme

messages.subject: Re: Multi-session mixture models with two detector types
parts:
I'm sorry but I can't see what is going wrong. When I try to match your problem with one of the builtin datasets everything works fine:

tempCH <- ovenCH
msk <- make.mask(traps(tempCH[[1]]), buffer = 200, nx = 20, type = 'trapbuffer')
# artificially change detector type of two sessions from multi to count
for (i in 3:4) detector(traps(tempCH[[i]])) <- 'count'
fit <- secr.fit(tempCH, mask = msk, hcov = 'Sex', model = g0~h2)
predict(fit)[1:2]

It may be an issue specific to your data. I am sceptical about using 'count' for camera data - the data are so sparse that 'proximity' would be just as good, without raising concerns about independence (if same individual ever recorded twice on one day at one camera). I would also find it tedious to treat every single day (?) as a separate occasion - that slows model fitting for no real benefit. You could at least collapse the count data with 'reduce(by...)' until you get it working. Judging from your use of 'autoini' you have had some trouble with starting values, and that may still be where the problem lies.

Can you see how your data might differ significantly from the ovenbird data? It would help to reproduce the problem with that dataset, or to generate a simpler reproducible example.
Murray
